story.title: Where the Mountains Meet the Harbor: Inside the Al Yazan Waterfront Vision for Port Sultan Qaboos in Muttrah
story.seo_title: Al Yazan Waterfront Project Unveiled at Port Sultan Qaboos
story.meta_description: OMRAN Group and VA Group announce the 18.5-hectare Al Yazan Integrated Tourism Complex along the Port Sultan Qaboos waterfront in Muttrah, Muscat.

detail.extracted_title: Where the Mountains Meet the Harbor: Inside the Al Yazan Waterfront Vision for Port Sultan Qaboos in Muttrah
detail.excerpt: Spanning 18.5 hectares along the historic harbor, the newly announced Al Yazan Integrated Tourism Complex steps down from the surrounding crags toward a 400-meter coastal promenade, crescent amphitheater, and 30,000 square meters of green space.
detail.article_html:
Anyone who has walked the curve of the Muttrah Corniche knows how closely the rock and the water press together here. Dark ophiolite hills rise almost directly behind whitewashed merchant houses, while wooden dhows and modern vessels share the sheltered basin of Port Sultan Qaboos. Any new architecture added to this coastline has to answer to both the steep mountain slopes and the open harbor.

Yesterday, under the patronage of His Highness Sayyid Bilarab bin Haitham Al Said, Minister of State and Governor of Muscat, Oman Tourism Development Company (OMRAN Group) and VA Group announced the launch of the Al Yazan Integrated Tourism Complex along the Port Sultan Qaboos waterfront in the Wilayat of Muttrah. Covering approximately 18.5 hectares, the project introduces roughly 1,500 residential units alongside public walkways, parks, and cultural gathering spaces.

Architecture That Steps Down From the Crags to the Sea

Rather than placing uniform high-rises along the water's edge, the master plan for Al Yazan takes its cue from Muttrah's historic urban fabric. Across three development phases, approximately 180,000 square meters of residential space will step gradually down the natural levels of the mountain foothills toward the shoreline, opening sightlines to the sea and weaving landscaped terraces between the buildings.

At ground level, the waterfront is designed around pedestrian life and community access. A seafront promenade stretches more than 400 meters along the harbor, paired with a dedicated pedestrian street housing 25,000 square meters of retail shops, cafes, and restaurants. Across the site, 30,000 square meters of green spaces connect the terraced residences to a crescent-shaped public plaza featuring an open-air amphitheater, multi-use sports courts, and dedicated play areas for children.

Public-Private Partnership on a Historic Coastline

Speaking on the launch, Eng. Ayad bin Ali Al Balushi, Chief Executive Officer of OMRAN Group, noted that Al Yazan marks a major step in the broader revitalization of the Port Sultan Qaboos waterfront in Muttrah. By adding a permanent residential and community layer to the harbor, the project aims to attract quality private investment and create long-term economic and social value for the capital's tourism landscape.

Roman Kapinos, Managing Partner of VA Group, pointed to Oman's stability, cultural identity, and the clear direction of Oman Vision 2040 as the foundation for the group's decision to invest in Muscat. For the people of Muttrah and visitors arriving along the coast, Al Yazan promises to turn an industrial port edge into a walkable neighborhood where mountain paths, public plazas, and harbor breezes meet.

detail.instagram_caption:
Along the sheltered curve of Port Sultan Qaboos in Muttrah, dark ophiolite crags rise directly behind the historic harbor. Yesterday, under the patronage of His Highness Sayyid Bilarab bin Haitham Al Said, Minister of State and Governor of Muscat, OMRAN Group and VA Group unveiled the "Al Yazan" Integrated Tourism Complex, an 18.5-hectare waterfront neighborhood designed to step down from those mountain slopes to the sea.

Drawing its architectural language from Muttrah's coastal heritage, the project encompasses approximately 1,500 residential units across 180,000 square meters of residential space built over three phases. Rather than walling off the shoreline, the master plan opens the harbor edge with a 400-meter coastal promenade, a pedestrian commercial street featuring 25,000 square meters of cafes, restaurants, and shops, and 30,000 square meters of landscaped green spaces.

At the heart of the waterfront, a crescent-shaped public plaza will host an open-air amphitheater, multi-use sports courts, and children's play zones, connecting Muttrah's residents and visitors directly to the life of the port.
